reason: Carbon dioxide can dissolve in rainwater, making it more effective at weathering rock.
expectation: The water will take up carbon dioxide and become suitable for weathering basalt.

effect: The rain is mildly acidic and can now act on susceptible minerals in the basalt.
reaction: The distinction between gradual weathering and instant dissolution is useful.
reason: The acidic rain can weather the young basaltic crust.
expectation: The rain will react with basalt and release some dissolved material.

effect: Water has altered basalt and released dissolved constituents; runoff may carry them toward the sea.
reaction: It is useful to see weathering occur without soil or organisms.
reason: Runoff is the likely route for carrying material released from the basalt toward the basin.
expectation: The runoff will carry weathered material away from the rock.

effect: The runoff now carries dissolved ions from the weathered basalt toward the basin.
reaction: The contrast between clear water and the material it carries is useful.
reason: The runoff can deliver its dissolved material to the existing sea.
expectation: The dissolved ions will enter the sea.

effect: The sea has received dissolved minerals, completing the first goal. The remaining goal concerns sediment.
reaction: The distinction between dissolved minerals and finished salt is useful.
reason: The altered basalt may also provide particles for sediment, so checking its available combinations could reveal the next route.
expectation: I expect to find a way to produce or transport solid weathered material.

effect: The inspection automatically loosened fine solid particles from the altered basalt, providing material for the sediment goal.
reaction: The distinction between transported particles and dissolved ions is useful.
reason: Runoff can carry the loosened particles toward the sea.
expectation: The runoff will transport the fine particles toward the basin.

effect: The runoff now carries suspended solid sediment toward the coast.
reaction: The contrast between cloudy suspended particles and dissolved material is clear.
reason: Sheltered water should slow the runoff enough for fine sediment to settle.
expectation: The suspended particles will settle as fine sediment.

effect: The suspended particles settled in sheltered water, completing the sediment goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the solid material settle after following the dissolved material into the sea.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following weathered basalt along both dissolved and solid routes was worthwhile because it clarified how water transports different kinds of material.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive transport steps felt a little predictable, although they made the routes clear.

surprise.text: Clear-looking runoff can carry dissolved ions, while cloudy runoff carries suspended solids; the two loads behave differently.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; inspecting the altered basalt revealed the particle route when I was unsure what to do next.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how the sea and its surroundings change further, especially if later combinations explain processes as clearly as the weathering and sediment routes.
